basic_usage.name: Basic Usage
basic_usage.description: Essential patterns for getting started with the greeting API

patterns.name: One-off greeting
patterns.description: Greet a single name without keeping any state

key_points: greet() constructs a Greeter internally, so there is no setup cost to manage
The default language is 'en'; an unknown code falls back to English rather than raising

antipatterns.name: Treating an unknown language code as an error
antipatterns.right_code: greeting = greet("Ada", language="zz")  # falls back to English
antipatterns.why: An unrecognised language code falls back to English and never raises. Code that catches an exception here is dead, and code that relies on one is wrong.

patterns.name: Reused greeter
patterns.description: Configure the language once and greet many names
patterns.code:
from greet_miri import Greeter

g = Greeter(language="es")
for name in ("Ada", "Alan"):
    print(g.greet(name))

key_points: Prefer this over calling greet() in a loop when the language is fixed
Greeter holds only its language, so instances are cheap and safe to reuse
explanation.performance_note: Greeter performs no I/O and allocates nothing per call; reuse is a readability choice, not a throughput one.

antipatterns.name: Rebuilding Greeter inside a loop
antipatterns.why: Constructing a Greeter per iteration re-does the language lookup for every name and obscures that the language is fixed for the whole loop.
